# Using the API

 ## Authentication
 Authentication is managed using an API key, which is provided to you. Every HTTP call to our API should contain a custom header called **X-APIKEY**. The value of this header must be the API key.

Here is an example of a HTTP request with the API key attached:
 

    POST /mgw/payment/hosted 
    Accept:application/json, text/plain, */*
    Accept-Encoding:gzip, deflate, sdch
    Accept-Language:en-US,en;q=0.8,nl;q=0.6
    Connection:keep-alive
    Host:https://sandbox.apexx.global/
    X-APIKEY:zJqFMRBDT8BPgkPO81UC0js2TWoFK

 ## HTTPS connections
 To ensure the security of our systems and adhere to industry best practices, at least TLS 1.2 is required for all HTTPS connections.
 ## Currencies and Amounts
 To make our platform support all currencies and to prevent rounding errors, amounts are stored as natural numbers, paired with an exponential. This exponential defines at which position the decimal point/comma is placed, counting from the right.
 

 Say we have an amount of £14.08 GBP. It will be stored and presented as 1408 with an exponential of 2. Some currencies, like the Japanese Yen, have no exponential. A transaction amount of ¥1,000 JPY is stored as 1000.
 ## BNPL Web Component
 BNPL Web Component - Merchant Integration  
 

Steps for Implementation --   
 

The BNPL Web component uses a custom HTML tag to display the Pay Later Options button on the checkout page.  
 

●	To initialise add the JavaScript web component dependency to your page as shown below :
 

    <script type="text/javascript" src="bnpl.js"></script>  
 

●	Add a BNPL web component custom HTML tag on your page:
 

 The button title and the merchant logo can be customised outside the BNPL Web component. You can use the title and icon attribute provided with the HTML tag <ce-payment> to use the name and icon as per the merchant’s requirement.

●	Response from the API call
 

The API call will respond after validating the request payload 
 

 Response is an object containing the following properties:
 

 id: uuid to fetch the payment partner list for the merchant.
 

 error contains details of potential error messages which are displayed using a toast/snack bar on the UI.
 

 There are two potential cases that you need to handle based on these response flags: 
 

 Positive response: Set the id from the response as an attribute to the custom HTML tag, this will make the Pay Later Options button visible 
 

    .then((data) => {  
 
      const payment = document.querySelector('ce-payment') 
 
      payment.setAttribute('uuid', data.id); 
 
      return data.id; 
 
      }) 
 

 Negative response: Pay Later Options button not offered, button is not made visible, and error is displayed to the user using toast message on the top right corner

Retrieve BNPL Providers List 
 

After the Button is Visible Users can click the button to get the list of Providers that are configured against the Merchant  
 
	  
 

Payment  
 

Clicking on any of the provider will be redirected to the Providers login screen where users can enter their credentials and proceed with the payment process  
 

Once the process is completed then Apexx will redirect to the merchants return_url(success, pending, cancelled) sent as per the bnpl/hosted API and send the response data in a Post request  
 ## Environments
 Apexx allows you to connect with two different environments for your integration. 

| Environment  | Endpoint   | Description |
|------|--------|-------|
| Sandbox  | https://sandbox.apexx.global/ | This environment provides you with full access to all the features available. Transactions will have no financial impact. |
| Production | https://liveapi.apexx.global/ | This environment will be the Live environment with access based on your configuration. Transactions will have financial impact. |
## Statuses
 <details onmouseover="" style="cursor: pointer;"><summary>Payment Statuses</summary>Payment statuses are returned as a part of Payment requests. 

| Status  | Description   |
|------|--------|
| AUTHORISED  | The transaction has been authorised by the acquirer, and can now be processed. AUTHORISED transaction status can either be captured or cancelled. |
| CAPTURED  | The transaction has been queued for processing. This request can be cancelled. |
| SETTLED  | The transaction has been successfully processed. The transaction can now be refunded. |
| REFUNDED  | The transaction has been successfully refunded and will not allow any further processing unless partial refund was requested. |
| FAILED  | The transaction has been rejected by us, or an error has occurred during transaction processing, most likely because the transaction request is malformed or inconsistent. |
| DECLINED  | The transaction request has been declined by the issuer. |
| CANCELLED  | The transaction has been cancelled and do not allow any further processing. |
| 3DS_REQUIRED  | The transaction has been enrolled for 3d secure. This transaction can be sent for authorisation after Authentication is completed by the customer. |
| AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED  | The transaction has been created but authentication is pending from customer. |
| CHARGEBACK  | The transaction has been charged back by the customer. |
| CHARGEBACK REVERSAL | The transaction chargeback has been successfully defended by the merchant and is reversed back to the merchant. |
| PENDING | The transaction has been queued for processing. |
</details> 

 <details onmouseover="" style="cursor: pointer;"><summary>Captured Statuses</summary>Captured statuses are returned as a part of Capture requests. 

| Status  | Description   |
|------|--------|
| CAPTURED  | The transaction has been queued for processing. This request can be cancelled. |
| FAILED  | The transaction has been rejected by us, or an error has occurred during transaction processing, most likely because the transaction request is malformed or inconsistent. |
</details> 

 <details onmouseover="" style="cursor: pointer;"><summary>Cancel Statuses</summary>Cancel statuses are returned as a part of Cancel requests. 

| Status  | Description   |
|------|--------|
| CANCELLED  | The transaction has been cancelled and do not allow any further processing. |
| FAILED  | The transaction has been rejected by us, or an error has occurred during transaction processing, most likely because the transaction request is malformed or inconsistent. |
</details> 

 <details onmouseover="" style="cursor: pointer;"><summary>Refund Statuses</summary>Refund statuses are returned as a part of Refund requests. 

| Status  | Description   |
|------|--------|
| REFUNDED  | The transaction has been successfully refunded and do not allow any further processing. |
| FAILED  | The transaction has been rejected by us, or an error has occurred during transaction processing, most likely because the transaction request is malformed or inconsistent. |
</details> 

## HPP - Customisation
 To allow you to maintain a consistent look and feel to the payment page we support customisation of certain aspects of our hosted payment page. The elements that are subject to customisation are defined below: 


    /* Frame Style - Start */
    @Frame-Font-Family: Poppins;
    @Frame-Border-Colour: #144056;
    @Frame-Header-Font-Colour: #144056;
    @Frame-Header-Background-Colour: #F1F1F1;
    @Frame-Body-Font-Colour: #144056;
    @Frame-Body-Font-Weight: normal;  /* e.g. bold, normal, numeric (like 100) etc.*/
    @Frame-Body-Background-Colour: #F1F1F1;
    @Frame-Text-Box-Border-Colour: #144056;
    @Pay-Button-Background-Colour: #144056;
    @Pay-Button-Font-Colour: #FFFFFF;
    /* Frame Style - End */
    
    /* HTML Body Style - Start */
    @Body-Font-Family: Poppins;
    @Body-Border-Colour: #144056;
    @Body-Font-Colour: #144056;
    @Body-Background-Colour: #FFFFFF;
    /* HTML Body Style - End */
    
 You can also customise whether you want to show order summary in the iframe or not by sending show_order_summary value as true or false. True will load the order summary in the page and false will hide it.
 
 ## HPP-iFrame  
 
 In order to load the Apexx HPP into the iFrame, you need to hit the **[Hosted Payment Page](#operation/hostedPayUsingPOST)** API with the necessary details. You will get the URL of the HPP Page in response. That url needs to be loaded into the iFrame object.  
 See below code snippet  : 
 

    <iframe src= "url"></iframe>  
 
 Once it’s loaded properly, you need to enter card details for further payment processing. After hitting the Pay button, it will go to the respective acquirer for the payment. Once the payment is done then Apexx will redirect to the merchant return_url as per **[Hosted Payment Page](#operation/hostedPayUsingPOST)**  API and send data in a POST request. 
 ## HPP-Redirect Return URL Parameters 
 Once the payment is done via Hosted Payment then Apexx will redirect to the merchant return_url with the below data in a POST request. 

    {  
     	"reason_code" : "string" 
    	"reason_message" : "string" 
    	"response_code" : "string" 
    	"response_message" : "string" 
    	"_id" : "string" 
    	"status" : "string"
    	"authorisation_code" : "string" 
    	"merchant_reference" : "string" 
    	"amount" : "string" 
    	"card_number" : "string" 
    	"expiry_month" : "string" 
    	"expiry_year" : "string" 
    	"token" : "string" 
    	"risk_score" : "string" 
    	"risk_provider" : "string" 
    	"risk_status" : "string" 
		"signature" : "string" 
    } 
    
 **NOTE :** A reason message is assigned by the acquiring platform. The Reason message will return only in case of a Failed or Declined transaction. Response code is sent only when the source of the response looks suspicious. In this case Apexx immediately cancels the transaction placed with the gateway.

 **[HMAC Signature Calculation](#section/Using-the-API/HPP-Redirect-Return-URL-Parameters)**

 The following steps outline the HMAC Signature Calculation process in Java which can be followed to validate the authenticity of a redirect POST request from APEXX after the processing of payments using the APEXX Hosted Payment Page (HPP). For this example, we have used the following Secret Key and sample JSON key-value pairs in order to generate the HMAC Signature. 

 **Example data**

 Example Secret key:

    8b29eeafeb554fd39c3ef9e21ef32c6a  

 Example JSON:

    {  
    	"reason_code": "0",  
    	"expiry_month": "12",  
    	"amount": "560",  
    	"card_number": "454305XXXXXX9982",  
    	"authorization_code": "654321",  
    	"merchant_reference": "3153",  
    	"_id": "89fce6908fc94bf78b50385701250355",  
    	"expiry_year": "20",  
    	"status": "AUTHORISED"  
    }  

 Example Map (Converted from above JSON):

    	Map<String, String> pairs = new HashMap<>();  
    	pairs.put("reason_code", "0");  
    	pairs.put("expiry_month", "12");  
    	pairs.put("amount", "560");  
    	pairs.put("card_number", "454305XXXXXX9982");  
    	pairs.put("authorization_code", "654321");  
    	pairs.put("merchant_reference", "3153");  
    	pairs.put("_id", "89fce6908fc94bf78b50385701250355");  
    	pairs.put("expiry_year", "20");  
    	pairs.put("status", "AUTHORISED"); 


 **Implementing the signature calculation**

 **1.**Sort the key-value pairs by key (Without Signature).

    SortedMap<String, String> sortedPairs = new TreeMap<>(pairs);  

 Example below reflects the sorting*: 

    "_id": "89fce6908fc94bf78b50385701250355",  
    "amount": "560",  
    "authorization_code": "654321",  
    "card_number": "454305XXXXXX9982",  
    "expiry_month": "12",  
    "expiry_year": "20",  
    "merchant_reference": "3153",  
    "reason_code": "0",  
    "status": "AUTHORISED"  

 *DECLINED/ FAILED transactions will also include reason_message in the signature calculation. We will always use all response parameters **(excluding signature)** for signature calculation. 

 **2.**Convert the sortedPairs into the JSON String:

    // Convert sortedPairs to JSON String  
    final ObjectMapper objectMapper = new ObjectMapper();  
    objectMapper.setSerializationInclusion(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL);  
    String jsonString = objectMapper.writeValueAsString(sortedPairs);  

 Example below reflects the JSON String: 

    {"_id":"89fce6908fc94bf78b50385701250355","amount":"560","authorization_code":"654321","card_number":"454305XXXXXX9982","expiry_month":"12","expiry_year":"20","merchant_reference":"3153","reason_code":"0","status":"AUTHORISED"}  

 **3.**Calculate the HMAC with the signing string, in binary representation given the UTF-8 charset, using the cryptographic hash function SHA-512.

    // Create an HMAC SHA-512 key from the raw key bytes  
    SecretKeySpec signingKey = new SecretKeySpec(UTF-8 secret Key, "HmacSHA512");  


    // Get an HMAC SHA-512 Mac instance and initialize with the signing key  
    Mac mac = Mac.getInstance("HmacSHA512");  
    mac.init(signingKey);  


    // calculate the hmac on the binary representation of the JSON String  
    byte[] binaryHmac = mac.doFinal(jsonString.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));  

 Example binaryHmac 

    [B@712f276c  

 **4.**Encode the result using the Base64 encoding scheme to obtain the signature. 

    String signature = Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(binaryHmac);  

 **5.**The signature calculated, for example, key-value pairs and HMAC key is: 

    OLyWcJi3RkhJNA6B+Ri2eYxzKprvTZtrR+diXecMEpsNFKGm6KBQ5flARez+OAc2Mac6HaPIJICJ29QhvblxHA==  


 **Verifying the Signature**

 In order to verify the signature to authenticate the HPP Redirect Return URL POST request, you must follow the steps outlined above and compare the output to that sent in the signature key in the POST request.

 Example POST request body including signature

    {  
    	"reason_code": "0",  
    	"expiry_month": "12",  
    	"amount": "560",  
    	"card_number": "454305XXXXXX9982",  
    	"authorization_code": "654321",  
    	"merchant_reference": "3153",  
    	"_id": "89fce6908fc94bf78b50385701250355",  
    	"expiry_year": "20",  
    	"status": "AUTHORISED",  
    	"signature": "OLyWcJi3RkhJNA6B+Ri2eYxzKprvTZtrR+diXecMEpsNFKGm6KBQ5flARez+OAc2Mac6HaPIJICJ29QhvblxHA=="  
    }  

 The binary representation of the JSON String should be used to generate the binaryHmac. The signature generated at merchant’s end should be compared with the signature received in the response.

 **NOTE :** Kindly be aware that the fields in the response can vary depending on the card scheme, payment methods, or particular scenarios. Therefore, it's essential to construct your signature calculation logic in a dynamic manner to prevent any discrepancies in the signature.

 **[HMAC Signature Calculation](#section/Using-the-API/HTP-Redirect-Return-URL-Parameters)**

 The following steps outline the HMAC Signature Calculation process in Java which can be followed to validate the authenticity of a redirect POST request from APEXX after the processing of token using the APEXX Hosted Token Page (HTP). For this example, we have used the following Secret Key and sample JSON key-value pairs in order to generate the HMAC Signature. 

 **Example data**

 Example Secret key:

    8b29eeafeb554fd39c3ef9e21ef32c6a  

 Example JSON:

    {  
     	"reason_code" : "0" 
    	"merchant_reference" : "3153" 
    	"_id" : "35363a63a56048ce9fbfd9e421a82c1b" 
    	"token" : "d98d6b21ac4a448abdda39fe65c3e457" 
    	"created_at" : "2020-04-16 15:07:17.0"
    	"card_number" : "454305XXXXXX9982" 
    	"expiry_month" : "12" 
    	"expiry_year" : "20" 
    	"card_scheme" : "visa" 
    } 
    

 Example Map (Converted from above JSON):

    	Map<String, String> pairs = new HashMap<>();  
    	pairs.put("reason_code", "0");  
    	pairs.put("merchant_reference", "3153");  
    	pairs.put("_id", "1d6b09b136304a2bbd842530bbc0b9c2");  
    	pairs.put("token", "d98d6b21ac4a448abdda39fe65c3e457");  
    	pairs.put("created_at", "2020-04-16 15:07:17.0");  
    	pairs.put("card_number", "454305XXXXXX9982");  
    	pairs.put("expiry_month", "12");  
    	pairs.put("expiry_year", "20");  
    	pairs.put("card_scheme", "visa"); 


 **Implementing the signature calculation**

 **1.**Sort the key-value pairs by key (Without Signature).

    SortedMap<String, String> sortedPairs = new TreeMap<>(pairs);  

 Example below reflects the sorting*: 

    "_id": "89fce6908fc94bf78b50385701250355",  
    "card_number": "454305XXXXXX9982",  
    "card_scheme": "visa",  
    "created_at": "2020-04-16 15:07:17.0",  
    "expiry_month": "12",  
    "expiry_year": "20",  
    "merchant_reference": "3153",  
    "reason_code": "0",  
    "token": "d98d6b21ac4a448abdda39fe65c3e457"  

 **2.**Convert the sortedPairs into the JSON String:

    // Convert sortedPairs to JSON String  
    final ObjectMapper objectMapper = new ObjectMapper();  
    objectMapper.setSerializationInclusion(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL);  
    String jsonString = objectMapper.writeValueAsString(sortedPairs);  

 Example below reflects the JSON String: 

    {"_id":"1d6b09b136304a2bbd842530bbc0b9c2","reason_code":"0","merchant_reference":"3153","token":"d98d6b21ac4a448abdda39fe65c3e457","card_number":"454305XXXXXX9982","expiry_month":"12","expiry_year":"20","card_scheme":"visa", "created_at": "2020-04-16 15:07:17.0"	} 

 **3.**Calculate the HMAC with the signing string, in binary representation given the UTF-8 charset, using the cryptographic hash function SHA-512.

    // Create an HMAC SHA-512 key from the raw key bytes  
    SecretKeySpec signingKey = new SecretKeySpec(UTF-8 secret Key, "HmacSHA512");  


    // Get an HMAC SHA-512 Mac instance and initialize with the signing key  
    Mac mac = Mac.getInstance("HmacSHA512");  
    mac.init(signingKey);  


    // calculate the hmac on the binary representation of the JSON String  
    byte[] binaryHmac = mac.doFinal(jsonString.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));

    String signature = Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(binaryHmac);

 ## 3DS  
 
This document describes how to enable 3D Secure authentication for card payments. The 3D Secure protocol is supported by several card schemes.
 
 3-D Secure authentication is an additional fraud prevention scheme that is available to all Merchants using the Payment Gateway.
 
 3-D Secure stands for 3 Domain Server, there are 3 parties that are involved in the 3-D Secure process: 
 
 - Merchant/acquirer 
 
 - Card Scheme 
 
 - Card issuer. 
 
 
 3D Secure transactions consist of below required steps:
 
 - **Enrolment ([3DSEnrol](#operation/cardPayWithThreeDSUsingPOST))**: Verifying whether the card supports 3D Secure.
 
 - **Redirection(redirect ACS_Url):** Redirects the card holder to an authentication page. A successful authentication creates an object(PaRes) that needs to be sent along with the transaction request.
 

	<form name="redirectForm" id="redirectForm" action="{acsURL}" 
		method="POST">  
		<input type="hidden" name="PaReq" id="PaReq" value= 
			"{paReq}"> 
        <input type="hidden" name="TermUrl" id="TermUrl" value= 
        	"{merchant_return_url}">  
        <input type="hidden" name="MD" id="MD" value="{psp_3d_id}"> 
     </form>  
 
    // Redirect customer to ACS_URL for 3ds_authenticate 
     <script> 
    	window.onload = function()  
    	{  
    	  document.redirectForm.submit(); 
    	};  
     <script>  

 - **Initiating the transaction ([3DSVerifyAuthentication](#operation/threeDSVerifyAuthenticationUsingPOST)):** Including the authentication object(PaRes) in the transaction request allows the transaction to be 3D Secure authenticated.
 
 
 **Enrolment request ([3DSEnrol](#operation/cardPayWithThreeDSUsingPOST)):** 
 
 If you want to request 3D Secure authentication for a transaction, the first step to take is to verify whether authentication is supported for the card being used. This is done by making an enrolment request ([3DSEnrol](#operation/cardPayWithThreeDSUsingPOST)):
 This request will return a paReq (payment authentication request), psp_3d_id (the unique identifier of initial Gateway response as MD) and a ACSURL (the 3D Secure authentication redirect URL) if the card is enrolled:
 
 **Redirection :** 
 
 If the card is enrolled, the next step is to redirect the customer on authentication page ACSURL served by the card issuer. This requires a GET or POST request.
 
 Below are the values that needs to be filled in while doing the POST request.
 - PaReq : Set this to the pareq parameter you obtained from your enrolment request.
 
 - TermUrl : The URL on your server to which you would like the customer redirected after a successful authentication. It's kind of return url.
 
 - MD :  A merchant descriptor reference that can be used to track the request. This will be posted unmodified to the URL that is specified in TermUrl. Set this parameter you obtained from your enrolment request as psp_3d_id. 
 
 After the customer successfully completes the authentication process, the 3D Secure server will make a GET or POST request to the URL you specified in TermUrl. The request body will contain the following values in POST request: 
 - MD : The unmodified merchant descriptor that you specified in your form. 
 
 - PaRes : The payer authorisation result, that is to be used in your authentication/authorisation request. 
 
 **NOTE :** If merchant is integrating with 3DS **Ingenico** using direct payment then the Implementation manager should be consulted by merchant. 
 
 **Initiating the transaction ([3DSVerifyAuthentication](#operation/threeDSVerifyAuthenticationUsingPOST)) :** 
 
 Send the Original Transaction Id (3DSEnrol response _id) and PaRes values in _id and paRes respectively as a new request to 3DSVerifyAuthentication API. If the authentication is valid, we will process the payment and respond with Success/Declined/Failure status.

The interval between attempts gradually increases with increase in the attempt count.

| 3  | 1 hour |
| 4  | 2 hours |
| 5  | 4 hours |
| 6  | 6 hours |
| 7  | 8 hours |
| 8  | 16 hours |

 ## Webhook v2 
 
### Overview : 

 
 
 Apexx uses webhook notifications for event updates. Webhooks are the HTTPS callbacks from Apexx that send event data back to your server. After setting up the webhook notification by providing the webhook URL, Apexx will send an update related to the transactions on the provided URL. Any update on the transaction will trigger a webhook notification. You should be able to accept the notification and send a HTTP 200 Ok response back to Apexx.
 

### Retry Mechanism : 

 
 
 Apexx will retry up to 10 times if your server does not send a 200 response back to Apexx.
 

### Webhook v2 Features :

 
 **HMAC Signature :** 
 
 Webhook v2 supports signatures so that merchants can validate the authenticity of the webhook received. Signature calculation logic is based on the HMAC SHA-512 algorithm, where a secret key is used to generate the signature. This signature key will be shared with you securely after the webhook is set up.

 ## CSE - Client Side Encryption 
 
 Client Side Encryption (CSE) is a card payment integration method that gives merchants full flexibility with how they present card collection fields to their customers whilst allowing merchants to minimise their exposure when it comes to PCI Compliance. CSE integration allows merchants to be PCI DSS compliant to a level of Self Assessment Questionnaire A-EP or above, in accordance with the latest PCI DSS standards (v3.2.1). Your particular level of compliance may differ depending on your own unique setup, so we recommend consulting a QSA to make sure you're set up in the right way to meet your desired PCI DSS level.

 Below are the proposed steps to implement Client-Side Encryption for APEXX merchants.

 **1. Encryption key** 
 

 The encryption key must be supplied to the Client-Side Encryption library and is used to encrypt the sensitive card details. The decryption key exists within a secure environment at APEXX. 

 **2. Include the APEXX CSE JavaScript Library** 
 

 For CSE to work, reference the APEXX CSE JavaScript library. The way to do this. Automatically reference the latest version of the current major release:

 **4. Implementation Of Data Encryption** 

 We can do the Data Encryption by below two ways: 

 **4.1 Implement the form** 
 

 a) For the form to work, use the “data-apexx” attribute for each item of cardholder data. A typical example is:

	<body>
		  <form action="[YOUR FORM ACTION]" method="post" data-apexx="payment-form">

 **Validate CSE fields**
 

 To ensure easy implementation of client side encryption functionality, Apexx provides internal javascript validations for the card details within client side encryption javascript. We provide validations for below fields 


 1. Card Holder Name 

 2. Card Number 

 3. Expiry Month 

 4. Expiry Year 

 5. CVV 

 You can utilise this functionality for all the fields mentioned above by calling respective functions in the javascript as mentioned below. 


 **1. Card Holder Name Validation :** 

| Field name| Possible Values  | Descriptions   |
|------|-------------|------------------------------------------------|
| Card Holder Name | Only alphabetic characters, Special characters allowed are (hyphen(-), underscore(_), dot(.), comma(,) and apostrophe(‘)) | It is representing the card holder name and it's optional field. |





 To validate Card Holder Name, Please pass the Card Holder Name in below function. 

	isValidCardHolderName([CARD HOLDER NAME);

 **Success scenario :** 


 If the card holder name is valid, in the response the error flag will be false i.e 

    {
   		"isError":false
    }



 **Error scenario :** 


 If the card holder name is not valid, in the response the error flag will be true and error message will display i.e 

    {
		"errorMessage":"Please enter valid card holder name",
		"isError":true
	 }



 **2. Card Number Validation :** 

| Field name | Possible Values  | Descriptions   |
|------|-------------|------------------------------------------------|
| Card Number | 12-19 Digit | Card number used for the transaction, also known as PAN. |



 **a. Characters Validation :** 



 To validate the card number, Please pass the card number in the below function. 

	isValidCardNumber([CARD NUMBER]);

 **Success scenario :** 


 If the card number is valid, in the response the error flag will be false i.e 

    {
   		"isError":false
    }



 **Error scenario :** 


 If the card number is not valid, in the response the error flag will be true and the error message will display i.e 

    {
		"errorMessage":"Please enter valid card number",
		"isError":true
	 }



 **b. Card Number Validation with Luhn check:** 



 To validate card number with Luhn Check, Please pass the card number in the below function. 

	luhnCheck([CARD NUMBER]);

 **Success scenario :** 


 If the sent card number passes Luhn check, response will contain error flag with value as false i.e. 

    {
   		"isError":false

 **Error scenario :** 


 If the card number fails Luhn check, response will contain error flag with value as true and error message will display i.e 

    {

 ## Appendix A - Formatting Restrictions,Data Type Definitions, Numbered Elements, Request Fields, Response Fields 

 
### Formatting Restrictions

 
 Unless otherwise noted, all field names are case sensitive and all fields accept special characters such as @, #, and %. 

 The value of amount and similar fields must not contain any alphabets or special characters. 

 The values of all request fields must not contain newline or carriage returns. However, they can contain embedded spaces and any other printable characters. All leading and trailing spaces will be removed. 

 **Data Type Definitions** 

| Data Type | Descriptions |
|------|-------------|
| Integer/Number | Whole number …, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, …}. |
| String | A string is a sequence of characters such as letters, numbers, spaces and special characters. String values must be surrounded by double quotes |
| Boolean | A Boolean data type accepts only one of the two values true or false. |

 


 **Array Elements** 

 The Apexx schema includes several array elements. These array elements are used to send or receive multiple elements of similar nature. For example, when a customer order includes more than one item, you must include multiple item elements in your request. Multiple item elements will be automatically considered as numbered elements by Apexx. So the value received in the first array would be considered as 0 and the second array would be considered as 1. These numbers are used to provide error feedback. 
 

 **Request Value** 

	"items": [ 
 		{ 
 			 "net_unit_price": 100, 
 			 "gross_unit_price": 100, 
 			 "quantity": 5 
 		}, 
 		{ 
 			 "net_unit_price": 100, 
 			 "gross_unit_price": 100, 
 			 "quantity": "abc" 
 		} 
 	]

    	  "code": "215", 
		  "details": "items[1].quantity", 
		  "message": "Quantity is invalid or missing.", 
		  "timestamp": 1614057343744,

 ## Appendix C - CVV Responses, AVS Responses 
 
### CVV Responses
 CVV results are returned as a part of Payment requests. 

| Code  | Description   |
|------|--------|
| D  | Suspicious transaction |
| I  | The CVN failed the processor's data validation check. |
| M  | CVV Matched |
| N  | CVV does not match |
| P  | CVN not processed for unspecified reason |
| S  | CVN not included in request |
| U  | Card verification is not supported |
| X  | Card verification is not supported by the payment card company. |
| Y  | CVN failed the processor's data validation check |
| 0  | No service available |
| 1  | Card verification is not supported for this processor or card type. |
| 2  | An unrecognized result code was returned by the processor for the card verification response. |
| 3  | No result code was returned by the processor. |

<br>

tags.description:
JavaScript SDK Integration 1.0.0

The Apexx Payment Integration SDK is a comprehensive solution designed to streamline payment processing for merchants by integrating multiple payment methods into a single, unified platform. With support for providers like PayPal, Volt, and others, the SDK enables merchants to offer their customers a diverse range of payment options while ensuring seamless management of the payment flow tailored to each method.

What is this Library for?

The Apexx-PayPal SDK is designed to simplify the integration of PayPal's Embedded Checkout into web applications. This SDK abstracts the complexities of payment logic, enabling merchants to easily handle payment approval and event-driven callbacks. The SDK allows customization of funding sources such as PayPal and Volt, providing flexibility for developers and businesses alike. This document outlines the SDK’s core design, focusing on its key methods, error-handling strategy, and security considerations. By using this SDK, developers can streamline the integration of Apexx's payment services within their applications.

What are the features?

  • Paypal
    • Express Checkout
    • Pay Later
    • Credit

Use Cases

  • Online Payments & Checkout
    • Integrate PayPal Express Checkout for faster transactions.
    • Accept Pay Later and Paypal Credits
  • Option to auto-capture or capture later.
  • Option to complete the order as per your flow.

SDK Process Flow

Apexx Completes the Order (CompleteOrder = true) Merchant Completes the Order (CompleteOrder = false)

How to setup?

The Apexx js library can be downloaded from here:
Environment Endpoint Description
Sandbox https://sandboxsdk.apexx.global/ApexxSDK.min.js This environment provides you with full access to all the features available. Transactions will have no financial impact.
Production https://sdk.apexx.global/ApexxSDK.min.js This environment will be the Live environment with access based on your configuration. Transactions will have financial impact.

Where to get credentials

If you already have a relationship with a service provider, we will help create the neccessary IDs and share them with your payment provider of choice. If you do not yet have an account with a payment service provider, please reach out to your Apexx account manager who will be happy to help facitlate the onboarding process. To process payments via Apexx SDK you will need an organisation id and an X-APIKEY which you can get from your Apexx account manager.

How to consume the library?

If you are consuming the library directy from our CDN (Recommended), then add the following JS snippet to your relevant checkout page. 
<script src="https://paypalsandboxsdkdemo.apexx.global/ApexxSDK.min.js"></script>
const paymentInstance = new Apexx("PayPal", (error) => {
console.error("Error initializing payment SDK:", error);
});

How to incorporate with any existing libraries

Merchants can integrate the SDK alongside their existing payment processing systems. The SDK is compatible with JavaScript and backend payment flows. Please note that any unique IDs that are used would need to be specific to the JS library.

How to make a call

Encrypting Payment parameters

Before initializing the SDK you would need to encrypt the data required for processing the payment. To encrypt the data you can call the Apexx server encryption API which will provide you with the required details to initiate the javascript SDK. For more details on server encryption API, visit API Reference The details of the fields required to be encrypted are mentioned in the schema definitions below.

Initializing the embedded element

Initialize the Apexx wrapper by loading the script from Apexx, using the activation instance keyword (e.g. "PayPal") and an error callback function to handle wrapper error for that payment instance. 
Eg: const paypalInstance = new Apexx("PayPal",(error)=>{alert(console.log("error"); ))});
The APEXX SDK is initialized using a configuration object that contains key parameters required for payment processing. The initialization process sets up the SDK environment and ensures all provided configurations are validated. Key Parameters & Data Type : These are needed to be provided as a single object.
  • encryptedkey (string) – Required
    • Encrypted Key received in the Get encryption API call.
  • encryptedpayload (string) – Required
    • Encrypted payload received in the Get encryption API call.
  • completeOrder (boolean) - Optional
    • Field defines whether transaction should be completed by the SDK or you want to complete it separately after the approval of the order.
  • organisation_id (string) - Required
    • The ID of an organisation.
Example 
const apexx = new Apexx({
encryptedkey: 'eyJraWQiOiJnM2FKMlJyUVNFYmM5WTVxUFowaDR0bVpr....', // Required
encryptedpayload: 'eyJlbmMiOiJBMTI4Q0JDLUhTMjU2IiwiYWxnIjoiZGlyIn0....', // Required
completeOrder: 'true',
organisation_id:'716ae509B5091A44baBaadeAc4b384e6b31d'
sources to enable eventHandlers: { // Optional event handlers onApprove: (data, actions) => {
console.log('Payment Approved', data); }, onError: (error) => {
console.error('Payment Error:', error); }, onCancel: (error) => {
console.error('Payment Error:', error); },}
});

Completing the order

You can pass the completeOrder field as true to complete the order from the Apexx SDK after the approval is received from Paypal. If you wish to complete the order from your side via a server to server call then pass the completeOrder field as false. However if you chose to complete the order yourself then you will have to call the Apexx Complete Order API which will process the transaction and respond you back with the transaction data. See Complete Order API for retrieving order details Please Note: If you are not doing an auto-capture then capture request will be required separately which you can find at below location. See Capture API Reference

Error handling

Error Categories

Use onError callback to handle errors dynamically. Log errors to capture debugging information.
Error TypeDescription
INPUT_VALIDATIONIssues with provided parameters.
SECURITYSecurity-related errors.
GENERICGeneral errors not categorized elsewhere.
SCRIPTIssues loading the SDK.

Error Messages

CodeDescription
MISSING_CONTAINERIContainer not created , Instantiate container first..
INVALID_FORMATInvalid {type} format.
MALICIOUS_INPUTDetected potentially malicious and sanitized.
GENERIC_ERRORError occurred during {type} operation.
SCRIPT_ERRORFailed to load {type} script instance.

Error Statuses

StatusDescription
INVALID_MODE400 (BadRequest)
MISSING_PAYMENT_CONTAINER500 (Internal Server Error)
INVALID_FORMAT400 (BadRequest)
MALICIOUS_INPUT403 (Forbidden)
GENERIC_ERROR500 (Internal Server Error)
SCRIPT_ERROR500 (Internal Server Error)
<script src="https://paypalsandboxsdkdemo.apexx.global/ApexxSDK.min.js"
integrity="sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxjwG6ODnY7XJ5SPPc4v5Z4tM""
 crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

Security considerations

To ensure a secure integration of the Apexx SDK, merchants should follow these security best practices:
  • Always load the SDK and make API calls over HTTPS to prevent interception of sensitive payment data.
  • Validate and Sanitize Inputs
  • Ensure that all user inputs, including payment details, are properly validated and sanitized to prevent injection attacks.
  • Use Apexx’s server encryption API to encrypt sensitive payment data before transmitting it to the SDK.
  • Use HTTPS when calling the api to encrypt the payload
  • Implement Content Security Policy (CSP)
  • Configure a strict CSP header to prevent unauthorized script execution.
  • Never expose API keys or encryption credentials on the client-side. Store them securely on your backend.
  • Restrict cross-origin access to ensure that only authorized domains can interact with your payment implementation.
  • Always use the latest version of the SDK to benefit from security patches and improvements. Handle Errors Securely
  • Avoid exposing detailed error messages to users, which could leak sensitive implementation details.

Y: Card enrolled or can be enrolled; you must authenticate. Liability shift.

N: Card not enrolled; proceed with authorization. Liability shift.

1: Cardholder is not participating, but the attempt to authenticate was recorded.

6: Issuer unable to perform authentication.

9: Cardholder did not complete authentication.

tra_exemption.description:
"This indicates that exemption from SCA is requested for the transaction. Valid values as mentioned below:

 ""external"" - Transaction risk analysis conducted by approved external source

 ""acquirer"" - Transaction risk analysis conducted by the acquirer

 ""scp"" - scp stands for Secure Corporate Payment

 ""lvp"" - lvp stands for Low-Value Payment

 ""delegated"" - Exemption indicator for delegated authentication.

 This flag specifies whether the transaction is exempt from strong customer authentication (SCA) requirements in Europe because the authentication was delegated to a different provider, such as an acquirer or payment technology provider (PTP)."

http_color_depth.description: Represents the bit depth of color supported by the user’s display environment. It indicates how many bits are used to represent the color of a single pixel, which in turn defines the range of distinct colors that can be displayed.

http_browser_language.description: The default language setting of the customer’s browser (e.g., "en-US", "fr-FR").Useful for localization, risk analysis, and understanding customer preferences.

http_screen_height.description: The height of the customer’s device screen in pixels (e.g., 1080).Often captured to verify the device profile.

http_screen_width.description: The width of the customer’s device screen in pixels (e.g., 1920).Used together with http_screen_height to describe display resolution.

http_time_difference.description: The time zone offset (in minutes or hours) between the customer’s local device time and UTC (e.g., +330 for IST).Helps in detecting anomalies if device time doesn’t match geolocation.

customer_ip.description: The IP address of the customer’s device at the time of transaction (IPv4 or IPv6).Commonly used for geolocation and fraud detection.

Identifies the content types the browser supports.

user_agent_browser_value.description: The raw User-Agent header string provided by the browser (e.g., Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)).Contains information about browser,OS,and device.

device_channel.description:
Specifies the channel through which the transaction is initiated (e.g., "BROWSER", "APP", "POS").
Helps in categorizing the origin of the request.For HPP and for javascript based transactions value should be BROWSER.
